text.Kredi Taksiti Bütçenizin Ne Kadarı Olmal: How Much of Your Budget Should Go to Loan Installments? - KredimGeldi
text.Aylık gelirin ne kadarı kredi taksitleri: How much of your monthly income should go to loan installments? A simple budget plan using the 50/30/20 rule, the debt-to-income ratio and an emergency fund.
text.Bir kredinin onaylanması, o krediyi raha: Getting a loan approved doesn't mean you can comfortably pay it back. Banks assess your income and credit history, but you know your monthly living expenses best. Making a simple budget plan before taking out a loan keeps you from struggling later on.
text.Önce gelir ve giderlerinizi çıkarın: Start by listing your income and expenses
text.Son üç ayın banka ve kart hareketlerine: Go through the last three months of your bank and card transactions and split your average monthly expenses into three groups:
text.Bu örnekte yeni bir kredi taksiti, mevcu: In this example, a new loan installment has to fit into the 10,000 TL share together with existing debt payments and savings. A higher installment means cutting back on discretionary spending.
text.Borç-gelir oranı = Aylık toplam borç öde: Debt-to-income ratio = Total monthly debt payments ÷ Monthly net income × 100
text.Kredi çekmeyi düşündüğünüz taksit tutarı: For two or three months, transfer the installment amount you're considering into a separate account every month. If you can do it without strain, the installment fits your budget; plus, these savings become a down payment or an emergency fund.
text.Bütçeye göre vade seçimi: Choosing a term based on your budget
text.Bütçeniz belli olduktan sonra tersinden: Once your budget is clear, work backwards: decide on the installment amount you can set aside, then see the shortest term in which you can repay the amount you need with that installment. A shorter term reduces total interest, but an installment that strains your budget increases the risk of late payments and damage to your credit score. Your budget determines the right balance.
text.Ayırabileceğiniz taksite göre tutar ve v: Try different amounts and terms based on the installment you can afford, and see the banks' offers.
text.Maaşımın ne kadarı kredi taksitine gideb: How much of my salary can go to loan installments?
text.Genel öneri, tüm kredi ve kart taksitler: The general recommendation is that all your loan and card installments combined should not exceed 30–35% of your monthly net income.
text.Acil durum fonu ne kadar olmalı?: How big should an emergency fund be?
text.En az 3 ila 6 aylık zorunlu giderinizi k: It's recommended that it cover at least 3 to 6 months of your essential expenses.
text.50/30/20 kuralı herkese uyar mı?: Does the 50/30/20 rule work for everyone?
text.Hayır, bir başlangıç noktasıdır. Gelir d: No, it's a starting point. The share of essential expenses can vary depending on income level and the city you live in; what matters is regularly setting aside a share for savings and debt payments.

html.<strong>Zorunlu giderler:</strong> Kira,: Essential expenses: Items such as rent, building fees, utility bills, groceries, transportation, school and healthcare.
html.<strong>İsteğe bağlı giderler:</strong>: Discretionary expenses: Spending that can be postponed, such as eating out, entertainment, subscriptions and clothing.
html.<strong>Birikim ve borç ödemeleri:</stro: Savings and debt payments: Existing loan installments, card payments and savings.
html.Bütçe planlamada sık kullanılan pratik b: A practical method often used in budget planning is to divide your net income into three: 50% for essential expenses, 30% for discretionary spending and 20% for savings and debt payments. These ratios aren't hard rules; in cities where essential expenses like rent are high, the split may differ. But it's a good starting point for seeing where you can cut back.

html.Tüm kredi ve kart taksitlerinizin toplam: The ratio of all your loan and card installments combined to your monthly net income is called the debt-to-income ratio:
html.Pek çok finans uzmanı bu oranın <strong>: Many financial experts recommend keeping this ratio below 30–35%. For example, on a net income of 50,000 TL, keeping total installments under roughly 15,000–17,500 TL leaves room to maneuver for unexpected expenses. With a long-term debt like a home loan, you need to pay even closer attention to this limit.
html.Kredi taksitleri her ay sabittir, ancak: Loan installments stay the same every month, but life doesn't. A job change, a medical expense or an unexpected repair can cause you to fall behind on your installments. Building an emergency fund that covers at least 3–6 months of essential expenses keeps you from taking on new debt at such a moment. Keep the fund in an account that's easy to access but separate from your everyday spending.
